passage:
Mariam: Can we talk about why the kids got one water break in a 90-minute practice on Saturday? It was 88 degrees.
Coach Greg: Honestly, the bigger issue is that a third of the team still hasn't paid the uniform fee. Let's get that sorted first.
Mariam: That's separate. I'm asking about water.
cue: the bigger issue is that a third of the team still hasn't paid the uniform fee
explanation: Coach Greg answers a question about water breaks in the heat by switching to unpaid uniform fees. The fees may matter, but they don't explain or justify one water break at 88 degrees.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: Greg doesn't misstate Mariam's concern; he skips it entirely and raises a different issue.

passage: You're asking why the heat was out for six days in January. What I'd like everyone to appreciate is that we just repainted the entire lobby and installed new mailboxes. Honestly, this building has never looked better. Okay, next question?
cue: we just repainted the entire lobby and installed new mailboxes
explanation: The manager responds to six days without heat by talking up the lobby paint and mailboxes. Those upgrades don't explain the outage or what will prevent the next one.

whyNot.fal_tu_quoque: The manager doesn't point at the tenants' own behavior; he simply switches to a more flattering topic.

title: Re: Homework load in grade 7
passage: Dear Mr. Abara, thank you for raising your concern about the amount of nightly homework in grade 7. I'll share your note with the grade 7 team. I'd also like to highlight that our grade 7 math scores rose 11 points this year, the best gain in the district. Our teachers are doing remarkable work, and I hope families feel proud of that. Warm regards, Lorraine Hughes
cue: our grade 7 math scores rose 11 points this year
explanation: The principal politely acknowledges the homework concern, then pivots to rising test scores. Better scores don't tell Mr. Abara whether the nightly workload is reasonable.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: She doesn't twist his complaint into something weaker; she steers the conversation to a different, more positive topic.

passage: We've seen your questions about why some customers' email addresses were visible to other users last week, and we hear you. Security is always our priority. Meanwhile, we're thrilled to announce dark mode, offline sync and 40 new templates, free for everyone! Update today and tell us what you think.
cue: we're thrilled to announce dark mode, offline sync and 40 new templates
explanation: Quillpad acknowledges questions about exposed email addresses, then jumps to new features. Dark mode doesn't answer what went wrong or whether customers' data is safe now.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: The company doesn't misrepresent the customers' question; it leaves the question behind for a happier announcement.

source: HOA president Glen Moritz · Cedarline Commons annual meeting
passage: Several of you have asked whether the 12% fee increase was passed without the member vote our bylaws require. I understand the frustration. Let me tell you what that money is doing: the pool filters are twenty years old, the clubhouse roof leaks every spring, and our reserve fund was dangerously low. These repairs can't wait, and I think most of you agree.
cue: Let me tell you what that money is doing
explanation: Glen is asked whether the increase skipped a required vote and answers by explaining why the money is needed. The repairs may be urgent, but that doesn't show the bylaws were followed.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: Glen doesn't distort the members' question; he swaps a question about process for one about need, which is easier to answer.

title: Worth it, and here's why
passage: Three months with the Driftway X2 e-bike. A few reviewers say the battery only manages about 20 miles, not the advertised 45. What they don't mention is that the X2 is assembled in a solar-powered factory and the company plants a tree for every bike sold. That's the kind of brand I'm proud to ride, so take the range complaints with a grain of salt.
cue: the X2 is assembled in a solar-powered factory and the company plants a tree for every bike sold
explanation: Nate answers complaints about short battery range by praising the company's green practices. Those may be good reasons to like the brand, but they don't show the range complaints are wrong.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: Nate states the range complaint accurately; instead of distorting it, he changes the subject to the factory and the trees.

passage:
Simone: The shop says the transmission repair is $3,200. Should we just do it?
Ade: Before deciding: the same report says it needs brakes and a timing belt within six months, about $1,400 more. That's $4,600 on a car worth roughly $4,000, so replacing it is the better deal.
Simone: Ugh, fair.
cue: the same report says it needs brakes and a timing belt within six months
explanation: Ade brings in other repairs, but they bear directly on Simone's question: whether fixing the car is worth it. Adding up the total against the car's value answers exactly that.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: The extra repairs aren't a distraction; they change the answer to the very question Simone asked.

title: Why the Westside pool closed early this summer
passage: The pool closed in early August because we couldn't staff it: we needed 14 certified lifeguards and had 8. Pay was the main reason. Neighboring towns pay $4 more an hour, and three of our applicants told us they took those jobs. Raising lifeguard wages is therefore the most direct way to keep the pool open all summer next year.
cue: The pool closed in early August because we couldn't staff it
explanation: Marcus answers the question directly, then turns to wages, which can look like a change of topic. But pay is the cause he identifies, backed by applicants' own reasons.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: The wage discussion follows a direct answer and explains the cause of the closure, so it addresses the question instead of dodging it.
